arxiv-2105-04207.title: Age of Information Aware VNF Scheduling in Industrial IoT Using Deep Reinforcement Learning Thanks: Mohammad Akbari is with Communication Department, ICT Research Institute, Tehran, Iran (e-mail: m.akbari@itrc.ac.ir) Thanks: Mohammad Reza Abedi is with the Department of Electrical Engineering, Tarbi
arxiv-2105-04207.creator: Mohammad Akbari, Mohammad Reza Abedi, Roghayeh Joda, Member, IEEE, Mohsen Pourghasemian, Nader Mokari, Senior Member, IEEE, Melike Erol-Kantarci, Senior Member, IEEE
arxiv-2105-04207.description: Abstract In delay-sensitive industrial internet of things (IIoT) applications, the age of information (AoI) is employed to characterize the freshness of information. Meanwhile, the emerging network function virtualization provides flexibility and agility for service providers to deliver a given network service using a sequence of virtual network functions (VNFs).

arxiv-2106-03858.title: Discovery and origins of giant optical nebulae surrounding quasar PKS 0454 − - 22 2020 Discovery and origins of giant optical nebulae surrounding quasar PKS 0454 − - 22 – 9
arxiv-2106-03858.creator: Jakob M. Helton, Sean D. Johnson, Jenny E. Greene Hsiao-Wen Chen
arxiv-2106-03858.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jakob M. Helton, Sean D. Johnson, Jenny E. Greene Hsiao-Wen Chen. We report optical integral-field spectroscopy in the field of one of the most luminous quasars in the z < 1 z<1 Universe, PKS 0454 − - 22, with the Multi-Unit Spectroscopic Explorer.

arxiv-2203-07746.title: Stress-testing the Resilience of the Austrian Healthcare System Using Agent-Based Simulation
arxiv-2203-07746.creator: Michaela Kaleta 1,2,†, Jana Lasser 1,3,†, Elma Dervic 1,2, Liuhuaying Yang 1,2, Johannes Sorger 1,2, Ruggiero Lo Sardo 1,2, Stefan Thurner 1,2, Alexandra Kautzky-Willer 4,5, Peter Klimek 1,2,∗
arxiv-2203-07746.description: Abstract Patients do not access physicians at random but rather via naturally emerging networks of patient flows between them. As retirements, mass quarantines and absence due to sickness during pandemics, or other shocks thin out these networks, the system might be pushed closer to a tipping point where it loses its ability to deliver care to the population.

arxiv-2212-01478.title: A data-driven uncertainty modelling and reduction approach for energy optimisation problems
arxiv-2212-01478.creator: Julien Vaes, Vassilis M. Charitopoulos
arxiv-2212-01478.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Julien Vaes, Vassilis M. Charitopoulos. Taking uncertainty into account is crucial when making strategic decisions. To guard against the risk of adverse scenarios, traditional optimisation techniques incorporate uncertainty on the basis of prior knowledge on its distribution. In this paper, we show how, based on a limited amount of historical data, we can generate from a low-dimensional space the underlying structure of uncertainty that could then be used in such optimisation frameworks.

arxiv-2303-16590.title: High Energy Particle Collisions in the vicinity of Naked Singularity
arxiv-2303-16590.creator: Kauntey Acharya, Parth Bambhaniya, Pankaj S. Joshi, Kshitij Pandey, Vishva Patel
arxiv-2303-16590.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate particle acceleration and high-energy collisions in the Joshi-Malafarina-Narayan (JMN-1) naked singularity, which, in the absence of an event horizon, allows infalling particles to turn back under specific angular momentum conditions. These outgoing particles can then collide with infalling ones, enabling the JMN-1 singularity to act as a natural high-energy particle accelerator.

arxiv-2304-11996.title: Applications of Information Inequalities to Database Theory Problems Thanks: Research supported in part by NSF IIS 1907997, NSF IIS 1954222, and NSF-BSF 2109922.
arxiv-2304-11996.creator: Dan Suciu
arxiv-2304-11996.description: Abstract The paper describes several applications of information inequalities to problems in database theory. The problems discussed include: upper bounds of a query’s output, worst-case optimal join algorithms, the query domination problem, and the implication problem for approximate integrity constraints.

arxiv-2312-17058.title: On the optimality of Shapley value mechanism for funding public excludable goods under Sybil strategies
arxiv-2312-17058.creator: Bruno Mazorra
arxiv-2312-17058.description: Abstract In the realm of cost-sharing mechanisms, the vulnerability to Sybil strategies —also known as false-name strategies, where agents create fake identities to manipulate outcomes— has not yet been studied. In this paper, we delve into the details of different cost-sharing mechanisms proposed in the literature, highlighting their non-Sybil-resistant nature.

arxiv-2405-15653.title: Fourier–Stieltjes category for twisted groupoid actions
arxiv-2405-15653.creator: Alcides Buss, Bartosz Kwaśniewski, Andrew McKee, Adam Skalski
arxiv-2405-15653.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alcides Buss, Bartosz Kwaśniewski, Andrew McKee, Adam Skalski. We extend the theory of Fourier–Stieltjes algebras to the category of twisted actions by étale groupoids on arbitrary C ∗ \mathrm{C}^{*} -bundles, generalising theories constructed previously by Bédos and Conti for twisted group actions on unital C ∗ \mathrm{C}^{*} -algebras, and by Renault and others for groupoid C ∗ \mathrm{C}^{*} -algebras, in each case motivated by the classical theory of Fourier–Stieltjes algebras of discrete groups.

arxiv-2410-02585.title: Recovery of coronal dimmings
arxiv-2410-02585.creator: G. M. Ronca, G. Chikunova, K. Dissauer, T. Podladchikova, A. M. Veronig
arxiv-2410-02585.description: Abstract Context. Coronal dimmings are regions of reduced emission in the lower corona observed in the wake of coronal mass ejections (CMEs), representing their footprints. Studying the lifetime evolution of coronal dimmings helps us to better understand the recovery and replenishment of the corona after large-scale eruptions. Aims.

arxiv-2506-18601.title: BulletGen: Improving 4D Reconstruction with Bullet-Time Generation
arxiv-2506-18601.creator: Denys Rozumnyi, Jonathon Luiten, Numair Khan, Peter Kontschieder
arxiv-2506-18601.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Denys Rozumnyi, Jonathon Luiten, Numair Khan, Peter Kontschieder. Transforming casually captured, monocular videos into fully immersive dynamic experiences is a highly ill-posed task, and comes with significant challenges, e.g . , reconstructing unseen regions, and dealing with the ambiguity in monocular depth estimation. In this work we introduce BulletGen, an approach that takes advantage of generative models to correct errors and complete missing information in a Gaussian-based dynamic scene representation.

arxiv-2506-21616.title: TIM: A Large-Scale Dataset and large Timeline Intelligence Model for Open-domain Timeline Summarization
arxiv-2506-21616.creator: Chuanrui Hu 1 Wei Hu 1 Penghang Yu 2 Hua Zhang 1 Bing-Kun Bao 2 1 Qihoo360 2 Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Nanjing, China huchuanrui@360.cn huwei5@360.cn 2022010201@njupt.edu.cn zhanghua3@360.cn bingkunbao@njupt.edu.cn
arxiv-2506-21616.description: Abstract Open-domain Timeline Summarization (TLS) is crucial for monitoring the evolution of news topics. To identify changes in news topics, existing methods typically employ general Large Language Models (LLMs) to summarize relevant timestamps from retrieved news. While general LLMs demonstrate capabilities in zero-shot news summarization and timestamp localization, they struggle with assessing topic relevance and understanding topic evolution.

arxiv-2512-10505.title: Classical Dirac particle: Mass and Spin invariance and radiation reaction
arxiv-2512-10505.creator: Martín Rivas
arxiv-2512-10505.description: Abstract According to the atomic principle [ 1 ] an elementary particle has no excited states and under any interaction, if it is not annihilated, its internal structure cannot be modified. The intrinsic properties are the mass m m and the absolute value of the spin in the center of mass frame S = ℏ / 2 S=\hbar/2 .

arxiv-2512-18000.title: The Clustering of Little Red Dots from Ultra-Strongly Self-Interacting Dark Matter 2026 The Clustering of Little Red Dots from Ultra-Strongly Self-Interacting Dark Matter – References
arxiv-2512-18000.creator: M. Grant Roberts, Aarna Garg, Tesla Jeltema, Stefano Profumo
arxiv-2512-18000.description: Abstract We predict the effective clustering bias parameter, b eff b_{\rm{eff}} , at z ∼ 5 z\sim 5 for Little Red Dots (LRDs) seeded by Ultra-Strongly Self-Interacting Dark Matter (uSIDM). From our model, we find that b eff ∼ 4.5 b_{\rm{eff}}\sim 4.

arxiv-2606-04881.title: DiverAge: Reliable Pluralistic Face Aging with Cross-Age Identity Relation Guidance
arxiv-2606-04881.creator: Yueying Zou, Peipei Li, Qianrui Teng, Dianyan Xu, Zekun Li

arxiv-2606-17131.title: The flaring drill in the Galactic centre
arxiv-2606-17131.creator: Jaroslav Haas, Pavel Kroupa, Florian Peißker, Mark R. Morris

pmc-11345402.title: Carbon footprint analysis of wastewater treatment processes coupled with sludge in situ reduction
pmc-11345402.creator: Yiyue Sun, Yi Zuo, Yanjun Shao, Lihua Wang, Lu-Man Jiang, Jiaming Hu, Chuanting Zhou, Xi Lu, Song Huang, Zhen Zhou
pmc-11345402.description: The goal of this study was to assess the impacts or benefits of sludge in situ reduction (SIR) within wastewater treatment processes with relation to global warming potential in wastewater treatment plants, with a comprehensive consideration of wastewater and sludge treatment.

pmc-11423267.title: Navigating virtual selves: validation of the German version of the presentation of online self scale
pmc-11423267.creator: Lynne Marie Stöven, Philipp Yorck Herzberg, Fabio Ibrahim
pmc-11423267.description: The Presentation of Online Self Scale for Adults (POSSA), originally developed by Strimbu et al. is a well-regarded instrument for assessing online self-presentation. This study evaluated the factorial structure, reliability, and validity of the German adaptation of POSSA. A CFA analysis confirmed a satisfactory fit for the proposed three-factor model, as evidenced by a CFI of 0.

pmc-12512726.title: Sex-specific associations between household drinking water sources and depressive symptoms in middle-aged and older Chinese populations: evidence from one 8-year nationwide cohort
pmc-12512726.creator: Yu Wu, Lei Zhang, Yihao Zhao, Panliang Zhong, Shuai Guo, Xiaoying Zheng
pmc-12512726.description: BackgroundUnstable access to safe drinking water may harm mental health, yet its impact by sex remains unclear. We aimed to explore sex-specific associations between household water sources and depressive symptoms (DS) in Chinese middle-aged and older adults.Methods 5,868 participants aged ≥ 40 years were selected from China Family Panel Studies (2012–2020).

pmc-12584996.title: Dementia Caregivers’ Perspectives on Technology’s Place in Care Practices: Mixed Methods Survey
pmc-12584996.creator: Julia A Scott, Emma Cepukenas, McKenzie Himes, Kennedy Anderson, Kiren Grewal, An Mai, Sheila Yuter, Patricia Simone, Alicia Stone, Amaryllis Mavragani
pmc-12584996.description: BackgroundAs the number of individuals diagnosed with dementia continues to grow, collective caregiving capacity is simultaneously declining. As a result, caregivers often face significant stress and burnout, which negatively impacts both their well-being and the quality of care they are able to provide.

pmc-12698439.title: Meta-analysis of the efficacy of external application of Chinese medicine in the treatment of lower limb motor impairment in patients with post-stroke hemiplegia
pmc-12698439.creator: Jingwen Zhang, Xingyu Kang, Jiajie Niu, Jingwen Zhao, Siyu Chen, Shuai Shi
pmc-12698439.description: ObjectiveTo systematically evaluate the efficacy of external application of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)—including TCM plaster application, TCM iontophoresis, hot compress, fumigation, fuming and washing, soaking, hot ironing, and cold compress—in the treatment of lower limb dysfunction in patients with post-stroke hemiplegia.

pmc-12945102.title: The Effectiveness of Rehabilitation Interventions for Improving Leisure Participation Following Stroke: Protocol for a Systematic Review
pmc-12945102.creator: Serena Alves-Stein, Natasha A Lannin, Kylie Wales, Sharon Kramer, Laura Jolliffe
pmc-12945102.description: BackgroundLeisure participation is an important rehabilitation goal for survivors of stroke. Following stroke, there is a reduction in leisure participation; however, the focus of rehabilitation is typically on remediation of personal care activities and mobility. Furthermore, previous systematic reviews and current clinical practice guidelines provide inconsistent recommendations for rehabilitation interventions to improve leisure participation.

pmc-13069595.title: Prevalence of Delayed Breastfeeding Initiation and Its Risk Factors Among Reproductive Aged Women in Somalia: A Cross‐Sectional Study Using Somalia Health and Demographic Survey
pmc-13069595.creator: Nigussie Adam Birhan, Kefale Tilahun Getahun, Mahad Ibrahim Ali, Belsti Atnkut, Kindu Kebede Gebre, Tilahun Yemanu Birhan, Denekew Bitew Belay
pmc-13069595.description: Background and aimsAlthough the advantages of breastfeeding are well‐documented, many mothers struggle to meet the World Health Organization's recommendation for early initiation of breastfeeding. Improved cognitive development and intelligence in children are linked to early breastfeeding. As far as we are aware, no previous studies have looked at the initiation of breastfeeding in Somalia.

pmc-13077181.title: The Carbon Footprint of a Cesarean Section: A Study on Real‐Time, Prospectively Collected Data of Disposables, Energy, and Reusables
pmc-13077181.creator: Elisabeth Colenbrander, Eva Cohen, Florine de Haes, Niek Sperna Weiland, Wouter Hehenkamp, Dorien Salentijn
pmc-13077181.description: AimThe healthcare sector, particularly operating rooms, is a major source of greenhouse gas emissions. To reduce this impact, it is important to assess the carbon footprint of medical procedures. The aim of this study was to assess the carbon footprint of a cesarean section, focusing on CO2‐equivalent (CO2eq) emissions from disposable products, reusable products, and HVAC energy use.

pmc-13183035.title: Causal effect of urinary sodium-to-creatinine ratio on gastrointestinal diseases: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study
pmc-13183035.creator: Yan Jiang, Zhang Zhang, Yining Ding, Shuling Xu, Rumeng Chen, Zhiwei Zheng, Meihua Bao, Binsheng He, Sen Li
pmc-13183035.description: Given the epidemiological evidence suggesting an association between sodium intake and various gastrointestinal (GI) disorders, this study aimed to investigate the causal effect of genetically predicted urinary sodium-to-creatinine ratio (UNaUCr), a proxy for sodium intake, on GI diseases. Employing a Mendelian Randomization (MR) approach, genetic variants closely associated with UNaUCr were identified by extracting data from genome-wide association studies (GWAS).

pmc-13233190.title: Synthetic microbial communities: a novel emerging models for dissecting gut microbiota-host interactions in neurodegenerative diseases
pmc-13233190.creator: Pengya Feng, Wenqiang Zhang, Yonghong Zhao, Pengju Zhao, Enyao Li
pmc-13233190.description: The gut-brain axis (GBA) has emerged as a critical regulatory pathway underlying the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) such as Alzheimer’s disease and Parkinson’s disease. However, the high complexity and individual variability of native gut microbiotas hinder the precise elucidation of causal relationships between specific microbial taxa, their metabolites, and host neuroinflammatory or neurodegenerative processes.

pmc-13241461.title: An example of land-use relaxation and its effect on soil stabilization in the catchment of Lake Lavijärvi, Russian Karelia: insights from multi-proxy sediment analysis
pmc-13241461.creator: Mischa Haas, Fatemeh Ajallooeian, Natalya A Belkina, Dmitry A Subetto, Negar Haghipour, Caroline Welte, Carsten J Schubert, Timothy Ian Eglinton, Nathalie Dubois
pmc-13241461.description: Accelerated soil erosion due to land use is a far-reaching problem for today’s society. Soil degradation leads to outwash and redistribution of soil organic matter, which not only impacts soils but also adjacent ecosystems by downstream eutrophication of freshwater bodies.

pmc-13461003.title: Podoplanin-positive extracellular vesicles in ovarian cancer: linking thrombosis, platelet crosstalk, and cancer stemness – a narrative review
pmc-13461003.creator: Shreya Singh Beniwal, Rovena Tali, Samid Soeb Munshi, Yash Satish Caroicar, Zainab, Dina Mohamed, Aala Alhamsa, Yujin Jeong, Prashasti Dahiya, Rafael Everton Assunção Ribeiro da Costa, Chimuka Mwaanga, Aarushi Mishra
pmc-13461003.description: Ovarian cancer remains a leading cause of gynecologic cancer death worldwide, largely due to late diagnosis, frequent recurrence, and metastatic tendencies. Thrombosis is a common and life-threatening complication in these patients, contributing to poor prognosis and therapy resistance. Emerging evidence highlights a mechanistic link between tumor-derived extracellular vesicles and thrombotic events – particularly podoplanin-positive small extracellular vesicles (PDPN⁺ sEVs).

pmc-13501583.title: Dual trajectories of intrinsic capacity and frailty: a joint predictor framework for dementia risk in middle-aged and older adults
pmc-13501583.creator: Shuanglong Hou, Yi Pan, Xiongxiong Jing, Rui Liu, Jinjin Shen

pmc-13672409.title: Between scarcity and surfeit: a familial tale of contradictory iron disorders (β -thalassemia and iron-refractory iron deficiency anemia)
pmc-13672409.creator: Maha AlRiyami, A. AlSayegh, M. ALRawahi, J. Balasuburamanian, M. Rohlfs, L. Peterson, C. Klein, Y. Wali
pmc-13672409.description: β-thalassemia and iron refractory iron deficiency anemia (IRIDA) are distinct hereditary causes of microcytic anemia. Their co-occurrence in the same individual is extremely rare and complicates diagnosis and management. This case series emphasizes on the importance of performing molecular analysis to define personalized therapeutic strategies.
